```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)

library(tidyverse)
library(ggplot2movies)
```

# Movie dataset

[link to the description online](https://vincentarelbundock.github.io/Rdatasets/doc/ggplot2movies/movies.html)

The data contains:
- 58,788 movies (rows)
- 24 columns: 
  - Movie title 
  - Year
  - Length (minutes)
  - Budget
  - Rating
  - Votes
  - r1-10 (percentile per score 1-10, rounded to nearest 10%)
  - MPAA rating
  - Genre (action, animation, comedy, drama, documentary, romance, short)
  

```{r}
# This loads in the data from the package with the name "movies",
# But sometimes takes a while 
data("movies", package = "ggplot2movies")

# Alternative: 
movies <- movies

# Check data
dim(movies)
glimpse(movies)
class(movies)

# Remove whitespaces but retain the tibble format 
movies <- map(movies, ~str_trim(.x)) %>% as_tibble()
```
## Data manipulation

We have 10 rows for the rating (r1 - r10)

We have 7 rows indicating the genre of a movie, movies can have multiple genres. 

Create subsets based on the movie genres 

```{r}
movies_long <- pivot_longer(movies, cols = c(Action:Short), names_to = "genre", values_to = "genre_no_yes")
```
